text:
maya: quick check before i merge the router change — i flipped precedence so model_affinity wins over model_choice when a region_hint is present. can ppl scan for obvious contract/breaking issues? :eyes:

maya: current rationale: affinity is an operator-set preference (latency/cost tradeoff) and we observe it gives lower p50 for interactive routes in eu. test perf +15% p50, cost +2% for those flows. want to make affinity the tiebreaker when region_hint pins location.

maya: example requests (pre-change -> post-change expectation):
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model_choice": ["redwood/base-v1","redwood/alt-small"],
  "model_affinity": "redwood/low-latency-v2",
  "region_hint": "eu-west-1"
}
```

maya: pre-change served_model: "redwood/base-v1@eu-west-1" (model_choice[0] prioritized)
maya: post-change served_model: "redwood/low-latency-v2@eu-west-1" (model_affinity prioritised)

maya: compatibility notes: old clients may still send "preferred_model" — we map that to model_choice[0] for now. plan to add deprecation warning header when preferred_model present.

tom: why flip precedence rather than special-case the interactive routes? any safety/regression concerns?

maya: good q. we considered route-level override, but affinity is already plumbed as a per-request knob in the SDKs and customers expect it to be honored. making it global for region-hinted calls keeps observable behavior consistent across SDK/REST paths.

liam: do we have tests that assert served_model field shape? i want an integration clip that ensures served_model includes model_id + region tag, e.g. "<model>@<region>" so downstream logging parsers don't break.

maya: yes added unit + integration tests. snippet from tests: 
```python
assert response["served_model"].startswith("redwood/")
assert "@" in response["served_model"]
```

maya: also added a compatibility matrix in the commit msg mapping preferred_model -> model_choice and model_affinity -> affinity precedence flag.

eva: what about rollout? can we gate behind a feature flag so Dedicated customers can keep old behavior until they opt-in?

maya: plan: default flip for hosted API, feature flag selector.affinity_precedence=false for Dedicated customers. will wire console toggle and document rollout schedule. canary in eu-west-1 for 24h.

liam: please add a short eval to catch quality regressions: baseline on 10k prompts comparing tokens/cost + semantic similarity. ping @eva for eval datasets.

eva: ack — will provide the eval set by EOD.

infra-bot: automated-ci: router-unit-tests passed (3m 12s) ; integration-canary queued in eu-west-1.

maya: infra-bot, once canary passes i'll update release notes and send a heads-up to support and account teams (deprecation header for preferred_model).

tom: quick SDK note: JS/py SDKs expose model_affinity as an enum. add mention in changelog + bump minor. also ensure server returns a deprecation header: "X-Redwood-Deprecation: preferred_model will be removed 2025-09-01" if present.

maya: will add header. final question — any reason not to merge after canary passes?

liam: lgtm overall. make sure you add the integration assertion for served_model format and a unit that covers preferred_model mapping.

eva: +1 for rollout plan, will sign off after eval completes.

tom: +1 from me too. please add a short note to the API docs about precedence and example payloads.

maya: thanks all — will merge after canary green and docs + changelog updated. tagging this thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
